title: The middle card, without sorting
hook: To find the middle of 101 cards you could sort them all first. Do you have to?

knows: the median is the middle value in order
doesNotKnow: that you can throw away the side the answer is not on

misconception: To find the middle value you must sort everything first.
objective: The learner can explain that after a split the pivot is in its final place and the median lies on one side only, so discarding the other side finds the median of 101 shuffled cards in about half the comparisons that sorting takes, and that the saving over sorting grows with n.

claims.text: On these 101 shuffled cards (mulberry32 seed 38), splitting around first-card pivots and keeping only the side with position 51 finds the median in 8 splits and 297 comparisons.
claims.source: Builder node run of Demo.tsx split()/keep() logic over the seed-38 shuffle (selection sketch in scratchpad med.mjs), counting group size - 1 comparisons per split. Seed 38 is a disclosed choice: over seeds 1-40 the mean is about 292 for the median search and 640 for sorting, and seed 38 gives 297 and 619.

claims.text: The cards on the side that does not hold position 51 are dropped after each split and never looked at again.
claims.source: Demo.tsx keep(): lo/hi shrink to the kept side; split() only touches st.lo..st.hi.

claims.text: Each split puts its pivot in its final place, and position 5 is on only one side.
claims.source: After a split every smaller card is left of the pivot and every bigger card right, so the pivot's position equals its rank. CLRS 3rd ed. 7.1 (PARTITION), 9.2. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): Partition puts every smaller element left and larger right, so the pivot's index = its rank (CLRS 3rd ed. 7.1, 9.2).

claims.text: Sorting the same 101 cards with the same first-card rule takes 619 comparisons, about twice the 297 of the median search.
claims.source: Builder node quicksort (first-card pivot, group size - 1 comparisons per split) on the seed-38 shuffle: 619. Same Demo.tsx function sortCost(). Seed 38 chosen as typical (see c1).

claims.text: On 1,000 shuffled cards, finding the median this way takes about 3,300 comparisons against about 11,000 for sorting.
claims.source: Revision v2, rounded per fact-check pass 10. Expected values for first-card pivots on a random permutation: 3,336 for the 500th of 1,000 (Knuth's C(n,k) = 2[(n+1)H_n - (n+3-k)H_(n+1-k) - (k+2)H_k + n + 3]) and 2(n+1)H_n - 4n = 10,986 for quicksort. Builder's simulation (mulberry32 seeds 1-50, first 50 in order) gave 3,465 and 11,003, a high sample mean, so the stage no longer quotes it. Hoare, 'Algorithm 65: Find', CACM 4 (1961); CLRS 3rd ed. 9.2. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 14): Own node: Knuth formula for k = 500, n = 1000 gives 3,336.3; quicksort 2(n+1)H_n - 4n = 10,985.9. Own simulation (xorshift32, 20,000 shuffles, n - 1 comparisons per split as in Demo.tsx split()): quickselect 3,341.8, quicksort 10,987.3. 'About 3,300' and 'about 11,000' are right. Stage 9-card values 17 and 18 re-confirmed.

recall.question: You split a pile of numbers around a pivot, and the pivot lands in position 40. You want the number in position 25. What next?
options: Keep only the cards left of the pivot
recall.why: Positions 1 to 39 are all left of the pivot, so position 25 is there. The right side can be thrown away without looking.
